properties.name: A real local block device the store can hold an exclusive lock on — never a network filesystem
properties.spec:
REQUIRED, declared 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word. reflow2's single-writer guarantee is enforced by RocksDB's exclusive lock on the store directory, and that lock is only meaningful on a real block device or local volume.

⚠️ ON NFS THE LOCK STOPS EXCLUDING AND SINGLE-WRITER IS SILENTLY GONE — flo2's reflow2_updates.md states this as a hard constraint on their side, and it is the failure mode req:single-writer-graph exists to prevent: two writers against one store is precisely the corruption case. The failure is SILENT, which is why it belongs in the design rather than in a deployment note.

WHY IT IS AN INTERFACE RATHER THAN A CONSTRAINT: it is a contract somebody else must satisfy — the host, the orchestrator, the volume driver — and reflow2 cannot check it or enforce it. That is the shape of a required interface. Anthony chose to declare the environmental boundaries alongside the code ones (2026-08-09) so reflow2's hard requirements are computable rather than prose in a tracker.

MEDIUM `data` rather than a filesystem value, because the enum has none — the contract is a durable byte store with real exclusive locking, however it is presented.

IT ALSO BOUNDS THE HOSTING SHAPE: this container holds RocksDB open and cannot scale to zero. dec:open-hosting-shape-vs-long-lived-reflow2 remains open, and dec:stack-fly-staging-ci is scoped to api and web precisely because min_machines_running = 0 plus auto-stop would kill it.
